finding.summary: Gate 1b is unrequested scope well past the issue's stated Non-goal, and it changes who gets auto-promoted
finding.evidence:
The originating task (`docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md`, "Promote job: close mark-ready's exit-code chain (#937)") states its Non-goals as "No change to `mark-ready.mjs`'s behavior or its exit-code numbering. The script's contract is already what #929 pinned; only the consumer and the tests change." Its "Scope added after review" section enumerates exactly four post-review additions (identify CI by path, keep newest-wins, guard the trigger side, record `outcome`) — gate 1b is not among them, nor is the base-branch pinning or the head-re-read.

This diff nevertheless adds an entirely new promotion gate to `mark-ready.mjs`: `ciDefiningPathsChanged()` + `defaultBranch()` + `ranBaseCiDefinition()` (`scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:180-259`), wired in as `const ciDefinitionGate = ranBaseCiDefinition(prNumber);` and added to the `gates` array as "CI's definition came from main". The cost is operational, not tidiness: `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` includes `package.json`, `packages/*/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `knip.json`, so every dependency-touching agent PR — a routine class — silently loses auto-promotion, as does any PR whose base is not the repository default branch (stacked/agent-chained PRs), all shipped inside a fix for an exit-code `if`-chain. The behavior is documented in `docs/design/harness-engineering.md`, but not sanctioned by the issue this branch claims.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the working tree. Gate 1b exists exactly as quoted: `ciDefiningPathsChanged()`/`defaultBranch()`/`ranBaseCiDefinition()` at scripts/agent/mark-ready.mjs:205-282, evaluated unconditionally at line 284 and added to the promotion `gates` array at line 312 as "CI's definition came from main", where `gates.every` (line 325) turns it into a hard refusal (exit 1, PR left draft). The refusal surface at scripts/agent/checks.mjs:123-135 does include `package.json`, `packages/*/package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` and `knip.json`, so ordinary dependency/manifest PRs lose auto-promotion; the base-ref pin at mark-ready.mjs:244-249 additionally refuses any PR not based on the default branch (stacked/chained PRs). On the spec side, the originating todo states the Non-goal verbatim ("No change to `mark-ready.mjs`'s behavior or its exit-code numbering… only the consumer and the tests change", docs/tasks/active/20260825-promote-exit-code-default-todo.md:77-83) and its "Scope added after review" section (lines 47-76) enumerates exactly four post-review additions, none of which is gate 1b, the default-branch pin, or the head re-read. Gate 1b is described only in the lessons file (Round 4, lines 177-195) and docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1893-1946 — documented, but not sanctioned by the issue. No guard makes it unreachable, the code is present as described, and unrequested behavior change past a stated Non-Goal with an operational cost is squarely within the design-fit lens.

finding.summary: Third, semantically different glob→RegExp engine added where the repo already has one that interprets the very globs being mirrored
finding.evidence:
`CI_DEFINING_RE` in `scripts/agent/checks.mjs:140-153` hand-rolls glob→RegExp a third time. `scripts/changed-areas.mjs:56` already exports `globToRegExp` — and it is *the* matcher that interprets `harness.config.json`'s `ci.ciConfig`, the list `CI_DEFINING_PATHS` claims to mirror (`scripts/changed-areas.mjs:84 matchesAny`, used by `classify()` to compute `ciConfig`). `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:198` has a second copy, and `.github/workflows/ci-report.yml:217` a third — but that one is explicitly justified ("this workflow deliberately checks out no code") and is pinned against the module by `scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs:154`. `checks.mjs` runs with a checkout and already imports freely, so no such justification applies, and the new copy is pinned against nothing.

The two engines are not equivalent: `changed-areas.mjs` renders `**/` as `(?:.*/)?` (matches zero intermediate directories), while the new one splits on `**` and joins with `.*`, so `packages/**/package.json` would match `packages/a/package.json` in both but `packages/package.json` only in the former. Adding any such glob to `ci.ciConfig` therefore gives two different answers to "does this path define CI" — CI forces a full run while gate 1b waves the PR through. The direction of divergence is fail-open on a gate whose own comment calls itself "a REFUSAL surface, so a pattern that accidentally matched less is a fail-open".

verdict.reason: Every claim checks out. checks.mjs:140-153 does hand-roll a glob→RegExp engine (split on "**" joined with ".*", split on "*" joined with "[^/]*"), used by definesCi() (checks.mjs:156-159) for gate 1b via mark-ready.mjs:217. scripts/changed-areas.mjs:56-82 already exports globToRegExp and is the matcher that interprets harness.config.json's ci.ciConfig (matchesAny at :84-85, applied in classify() at :403) — the very list CI_DEFINING_PATHS mirrors (checks.mjs:98, checks.test.mjs:492-512). The two engines are genuinely non-equivalent: changed-areas.mjs:63-65 emits "(?:.*/)?" for "**/" (documented at :51-54 as deliberately matching zero intermediate directories) whereas checks.mjs:144-151 emits a plain ".*", so "packages/**/package.json" would match "packages/package.json" only in the former. The other two copies are accounted for — review-panel.mjs:198-208 is the shared helper (reused by hunt-gate.mjs:51, and named as a shared polarity-neutral helper in docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2440), and ci-report.yml:213-217 is explicitly justified ("checks out no code") and pinned against the module by scripts/test/ci-workflow.test.mjs:154-174. The new copy is pinned by nothing: checks.test.mjs:492-548 asserts only list-superset membership plus fixed sample paths, so a future "**/"-containing glob added to ci.ciConfig would satisfy the drift test while CI and gate 1b answered "does this path define CI" differently, in the fail-open direction on a surface whose own comment (checks.mjs:137-139) calls itself a refusal surface. No refutation ground holds: the code is present as described (not not-present), the existing test guards the list but not matcher semantics (not already-guarded), and duplication/reuse is explicitly in this lens's lane (not out-of-scope). Severity major vs minor is arguable since the divergence is latent rather than live, but that is doubt, which keeps the finding.
